structure.title: Causes and first campaigns
structure.text: The opening distinguishes stated disputes from deeper pressures, then follows decisions through speeches and military events.

structure.title: A widening conflict
structure.text: Later books trace changing alliances, civic breakdown, and costly ventures. The surviving account stops before the war's conclusion.

people.name: Athens
people.text: A democracy grown rich and confident on its fleet and its tribute-paying allies, led at first by Pericles, whom Thucydides admires.

people.name: Sparta
people.text: A cautious land power with a famous army and a society built around it, pressed by its allies to stop the growth of Athens.

people.name: Speeches
people.text: The speeches Thucydides gives his speakers, written as what the situation demanded, which set out the arguments behind each fateful choice.

context.title: Unequal alliances
context.text: Cities fight with different resources and degrees of independence. Calling a city an ally does not settle how freely it acts.

context.title: Reconstructed speeches
context.text: Thucydides explains his difficulty in recovering exact words. The speeches present the reasoning of situations rather than modern verbatim transcripts.

notice.text: Notice changes in the meaning of moral words.
notice.why: Civil conflict can reorganise what communities praise.

notice.text: Compare a policy's appeal with its outcome.
notice.why: Persuasion and competent judgment are not identical.

opening: Athens has wealth, ships, and good reasons to believe its power makes it safer. Sparta finds that power increasingly difficult to tolerate. Thucydides follows the war between them into assemblies where persuasive speeches become military orders and decisions made in fear acquire the language of necessity. He records plague, civil strife, and calculations in which another city's survival is negotiable. The unnerving force comes from recognising competent people, familiar arguments, and institutions under pressure, producing outcomes that almost nobody would have chosen at the beginning.
